resolutions.what_changed: `observe.page_text`'s docstring no longer says `frames=False` has no caller. It names `agent.check_state` (ADR-036) as the caller and says which half of the ruling routes through the branch: a Frame scope needs no flag (a Frame has no `.frames`), so the argument is exactly the main-document half. The `ponytail:` note is inverted rather than softened — it used to authorise deleting the parameter if T-M42-14 closed the other way, and now says T-M42-14 may take the two `page_changed` hazard bullets but may not take the parameter, because ADR-036 keeps a main-document-only read in `check_state` either way. The two hazard bullets are unchanged, as the acceptance asked: they are still true of the evidence pipeline.
resolutions.watched_red: None, and deliberately: a docstring cannot be graded red. The claim the comment made is now false-by-construction — deleting the parameter breaks `check_state`'s call, which every ADR-036 case exercises — but no case asserts the WORDING, and inventing a grep-for-a-phrase case would be a guard on prose that a rewording defeats.

resolutions.what_changed: ADR-036's declared cost is now measured. The new invariant case authors, on the committed `frames-swap.html`, exactly the shape the ADR said no case authored: a main-document `click` whose `expected_state.text_visible` names the FRAME's own text (`Document ID:`). It pins the whole ruling in one trace — the click resolves in the main document (`resolved.scope` = frames-swap.html), `page_changed` is true because the frame really did change, `postcondition_ok` is FALSE anyway, and then the declared recovery: the replan's page-wide `wait_for` (ADR-036's carve-out) verifies the frame and the `extract` resolves in `about:srcdoc`. ADR-036's Consequences bullet no longer says `No committed case authored that shape`; it states what the case pins, states the price (one extra replan on a legitimate frame-effect click) and records that the sentence it replaces was a declared limitation nothing could go red on.
resolutions.watched_red: Against the pre-ADR-036 mechanism, reproduced by passing `scope=None` at `check_state`'s one call site and changing nothing else: `main-document-click-cannot-verify-a-frame-only-effect  passed: False` / `checks {"status": true, "verdict": true, "recovery": false, "replans": false, "trace_postconditions": false, "resolved_scopes": false}` / `got {"status": "success", "answer": "NIMBUS-10K-2025", "reason": null}`. Page-wide, the click's postcondition is satisfied by the frame, so there is no failure, no replan and no recovery — four checks red at once while status and answer are green, which is precisely the trade-off made visible.

resolutions.route_taken: (a) fall back to page-wide, with the residual risk declared in the ADR
resolutions.what_changed: `check_state` gained one nested `live_scope()` that re-reads `Frame.is_detached()` on every settle pass and yields `None` (page-wide) once the acted document is gone; both predicates read it, so one guard covers `text_visible` and `role_visible` and both modes. Fallback rather than a loud failure, argued in ADR-036 §4: the hazard ADR-036 exists to close is a NO-OP verified by a decoy, and a detach is positive evidence the action did something (a `press "Shift"` detaches nothing), so that case cannot arrive through this door — while failing loud would kill a legitimate run on the shape M44's live target has. New fixture `src/browser/fixtures/frames-detach.html`: the button lives in an iframe, the click asks the host to open the filing, and the host replaces the pane — destroying the acted document and painting the result into the main document.
resolutions.watched_red: postcondition-scope-detached-by-its-own-action  passed: False / checks {"status": false, "verdict": false, "trace_postconditions": false, "resolved_scopes": false} / got {"status": "failure:act", "answer": null, "reason": "step 2 (click): StepError: expected_state not reached: {'text_visible': 'Document ID:'}; replan made no progress (identical or empty plan)"} — 2.55s, the full settle budget burned to reach the wrong answer. Green after the guard in 0.61s.

resolutions.what_changed: Logged, not fixed, with the finding's evidence and acceptance carried verbatim. The reason for routing rather than repairing: the ruling's cost is now measured offline by R2's case, so what remains is a prompt change whose effect is only observable on paid runs — a `full`-suite decision rather than a repair to land beside the mechanism.

One consequence surfaced here: committing `tasks/reviews/pr66-r1.json` puts the deleted report's NAME back in the scanned scope, and `report-citations-resolve` read it as a dangling citation. Added to `REPORT_CITATION_SKIP` (and to the case's `skip_exactly`, which pins the set's width) for the same reason the first literal is there — the name is the record of a removal, not a claim of evidence, and the alternative is editing a reviewer's verbatim text so a regex stops seeing it, which that code's own comment refuses.
